source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Simple allergies with no infectious or contagious component, contrary to the actual contagious, infectious nature of what this presentation suggests","B":"A normal cold requiring no further clinical evaluation, similar to what the parent is currently assuming given how hard the child is coughing","C":"Pertussis, a highly contagious bacterial respiratory infection, rather than the especially bad cold the parent is currently assuming this represents","D":"An unrelated cardiac condition requiring cardiology referral, which would not explain this particular cough pattern and whooping sound"}}
source_row.rationale: Severe paroxysmal coughing fits followed by a characteristic high-pitched "whoop" on inspiration, along with post-tussive vomiting, are classic findings of pertussis (whooping cough), a highly contagious bacterial infection preventable by vaccination, requiring prompt recognition, appropriate precautions, and treatment.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Pertussis Clinical Features and Diagnosis
source_row.stem: A child presents with severe paroxysmal coughing fits followed by a high-pitched "whoop" sound on inspiration, along with post-tussive vomiting, and a parent assumes this must just be a bad cold that happens to make the child cough especially hard.
